assessment.summary: BTK (Q06187) is one of the most comprehensively validated and druggable kinase targets in oncology and immunology. It has 170 PDB structures including sub-angstrom resolution ligand-bound co-crystals, over 21,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries, six approved small-molecule inhibitors (including both covalent and non-covalent classes), and nearly 1,000 publications with active ongoing research including next-generation PROTACs. Druggability confidence is exceptionally high across all evidence dimensions.
evidence_gaps: Resistance mechanisms (e.g., C481S mutation for covalent inhibitors) remain an active clinical challenge, and structural coverage of all clinically relevant resistance mutants may be incomplete
PROTAC/degrader structural data (ternary complexes with BTK, linker, and E3 ligase) are still emerging and may not be fully represented in PDB
Long-term safety profiles for newer non-covalent inhibitors (e.g., pirtobrutinib) in broader patient populations are still being established
Selectivity profiling across the full kinome for all approved agents is not uniformly available, leaving off-target liability questions partially open
Disease indications beyond B-cell malignancies and XLA (e.g., autoimmune diseases) are still under clinical investigation with less mature validation
